findings.message: The shared `commit_lock()` helper builds each `CommitLock` at a fresh `/tmp/chupa-test-<uuid>`. That path is hard-coded and sits outside pytest's tmp_path. Every `Git.add`, `commit`, `restore` or `merge_squash` in the integration tests and harnesses calls `acquire`, which runs `mkdir` and creates `commit.lock` there, and nothing removes either. Each `./dev.py test` run therefore leaves hundreds of directories in /tmp, and running the harnesses leaves more.
findings.paved_road: Have the helper take the directory the lock lives in, such as the test's tmp_path or the repo's `.chupa/state`, and pass it from each caller. If a caller has no tmp_path, root the lock under a directory pytest or the harness already cleans up. Do not hard-code /tmp.

findings.message: Acceptance 1 requires every git call `Git.commit(..., only=paths)` makes to run inside one hold, and both steps of `merge_squash` to run inside one hold. The fake `Lock` only records whether a lock was held when each call ran. It does not count enters or exits, so a regression that takes and releases the lock separately around `update-index` and `commit` would still record `True` for every call and pass. That gap between staging and committing is the race this ticket exists to close.
findings.paved_road: Have the fake lock count `__aenter__` calls, or record a hold id for each call. Then assert that `commit(only=...)` makes exactly one enter covering `update-index`, `diff`, `commit` and `rev-parse`, and that `merge_squash` makes exactly one enter covering `merge` and its commit.
